::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 23d 1861  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Westcountry Studies Library, Exeter/ Yonge 1861/14
:::

My dear [Miss Smith](people/person_263.qmd)

I have not the letter, at least I do not believe I have but I am almost certain that it was to be the 4 couples at 2lb; and I think you may safely so apply it. I will wait a week to write to [Mrs Elphinstone](people/person_482.qmd) in case you should be able to tell me anything specially about any of the people.[^1]

I do not know whether I forgot to finish my story or only put it stupidly, the point of it was the staring of the strangers at hearing such a grave polished man as [Dr Harris](people/person_629.qmd) proposing the worst street in Torr as an allurement to a lady. That Torr Churchyard is indeed a strangely mournful place, with all its records of early deaths among strangers and its graves so close together I wish we had more time to spend with the kind cousins there, but I was hurried away by having to meet [Mrs Selwyn](people/person_1297.qmd) before her return to New Zealand, and I could not go to Cockington though I have a whole houseful of cousins and a godson there.[^2] I did once walk there from Livermead many years ago.

[Masters](people/person_981.qmd)’s corrections and criticisms amuse me very much - it was great fun to see how he presided over the [Maiden of our own day](other_books/otherbook_315.qmd). I wish you would have a good fight with him it would do him good

yours sincerely

C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Letters to Carter Smith dated 18 March, 3 July, 21 November 1861 and 3 April 1862 refer to a donation by a Mrs Elphinstone of money to be given to poor people in Ann Carter Smith's parish.
[^2]: The Mallock family of Cockington Court were connected to the Yonges and the Froudes;  Livermead was a house at Torquay belonging to them
